title: OverSire app calls
description: A CLI command that the app runs (OVERSIRE-484). The CLI calls its local daemon. The daemon sends AppCallFrame on the WebSocket /v1/connect of the app on the same Mac (loopback only). The app runs the action from its action catalog and sends AppCallResult to POST /v1/app-calls/{id}/result. The app runs only the actions of its allowed list. Other actions give notAllowed. The daemon advertises the feature app-calls in DaemonInfo.features. A member call (OVERSIRE-528) is an app call from a client app: the client sends MemberCallRequest to POST /v1/member-calls on the home daemon, the daemon sends MemberCallFrame on the WebSocket of the source app of the mirror, and the source app answers with AppCallResult to POST /v1/member-calls/{id}/result. The daemon advertises the feature member-calls.

AppCall.description: One action for the app. action is an id of the action catalog, for example epic.list. args holds the args of the action. agent names the agent that ran the command. The events of a change name it as the actor.

id.description: The id of the call. The daemon makes it.

action.description:
A free string, an id of the action catalog. The CI actions are below (ci.json). A `ci.*` read action on a repo that OverSire does not track answers notAllowed.

ci.log: args {repo, jobId, lines?} (lines 1 to 2000, default 200), data CILogView (P1).
ci.jobs: args {repo, runId, attempt?, fresh?}, data CIJobsDoc (P1).
ci.workflows: args {repo}, data CIWorkflows (P1).
ci.refresh: args {repo}, no data. The app fetches the runs of the repo once (P1).
ci.rerun, ci.rerunJob, ci.cancel, ci.dispatch, ci.approve: args CIActionRequest, data CIActionResult (P2).
ci.explain: args CIExplainRequest plus runId, data CIExplanation (P3). The app runs the AI task on a cache miss.

agent.description: For example codex or claude. Absent: a human ran the command.

AppCallStatus.description: ok: the action ran. failed: the action ran and did not work. notAllowed: the action did not run (not in the allowed list, a bad arg, an unknown project or epic).

AppCallResult.description: The answer of the app to one AppCall. summary is one short text for a human. data is the JSON result of a read action, for --json.

AppCallFrame.description: The frame of the daemon on the WebSocket of the app.

MemberCaller.description: The app that sent a member call. The daemon fills it from the credential of the request, not from the body.

machine.description: The machine of the sender, for example mba.

name.description: The name of the credential, for example OverSire on mba.

device.description: The device id of the credential. Absent on loopback.

MemberCallRequest.description: The body of POST /v1/member-calls. action is an id of the action catalog. args holds the args of the action.

MemberCall.description: One action for the source app, from a client app. The result is AppCallResult. A refused call gives notAllowed. A settings conflict gives failed with data {"conflict": true}.

id.description: The id of the call. The daemon makes it.

cli.description: Set when an oversire command sends the call through a daemon. The app names the agent as the actor, via cli@<machine>. Absent: a click of a client app.

agent.description: <harness> <session>, as AppCall.agent. Absent: a human ran the command.

MemberCallFrame.description: The frame of the daemon on the WebSocket of the source app.

VendorRunArgs.description: The args of the app call vendor.run. The app runs the vendor CLI of an account with the token of its Keychain (OVERSIRE-567). Give exactly one of project and account. project is a project key and the app takes its tracker account. account is <provider>:<id> or <id>. args is the command of the vendor CLI with its flags, command first. cwd is the working folder. The app serves vendor.list and vendor.run only from the local CLI, never from a member call.

VendorRunOutput.description: The data of a vendor.run result. A vendor exit that is not 0 still gives status ok. truncated: the app cut stdout or stderr. timedOut: the app stopped the process (status failed, with this data).

vendor.description: The vendor CLI, for example plane-cli.

VendorCLIRow.description: One row of the data of vendor.list (an array). path is absent when the vendor CLI is not installed.

vendor.description: The display name of the provider.
